cells.tense: The bond is here, and how you hold it is being set right now.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When something presses against the closeness you picked — a doubt, a preference, someone else's worry — say once what this bond is for, then stop. Let the press pass without the direction moving.
cells.core:
Being close to someone is the whole work in this room, and what's here isn't a mood. It's a heading. You chose it, and the choice has held long enough to carry weight, which is why it can be named plainly and stood behind without a fight.

What the balance asks is small. When something presses against the closeness you picked, hold the line once — one sentence about what this bond is for, said in your own words — and then let the press pass. You don't need to reopen the matter because it got pressed, and you don't need to prove the choice to anyone. A direction you chose shows in how it holds when someone leans on it.

cells.verb: Choosing one bond and letting the rest of life arrange itself around it

cells.tense: Ahead of you the bond will be guarded before it has had a chance to simply be.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Notice what being close has already grown between you — a rhythm, a habit, a way of talking — and this week change nothing about it. Take it as it is. No improving, no next step.
cells.core:
Where closeness is the work, you're running ahead of it — guarding a bond before it's had a chance to simply be. The arranging, the anticipating of what could go wrong, the steady watch: it keeps the thing from being lived in, and it costs you more than it protects. Nothing here is falling apart. It only looks like it might from where you're standing, which is out in front of it.

Something between you two has been tended for a while — a rhythm, a habit, a way you talk when nobody's watching. This week, leave it exactly as it is and enjoy it. Don't improve it. Don't name the next milestone. The ease won't come from more guarding. It'll come from stopping.
cells.sheetLine: The bond doesn't need guarding. It needs to be lived in.
cells.verb: Choosing one bond and letting the rest of life arrange itself around it

cells.tense: The choice was finished, and you're still standing at the door it closed.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Put the pulls on you on one page — the people, the obligations, the shoulds — then go back and mark the ones you actually picked. Read your own handwriting once, no more.
cells.core:
Being close to someone is the work in this room, and you've stepped back from it. Not dramatically — the choice finished, and you haven't fully arrived inside it. The connection is there. You keep replaying the version where you didn't have to commit, and that replaying is what's holding you half out of the room.

Don't try to feel your way back in. Put the pulls on you on one page — the people, the obligations, the shoulds — then go back and mark the ones you actually picked. Most will be plain to you. One or two may surprise you. Reading your own handwriting, you'll see where the picking stopped and the drifting started, and that isn't a feeling to manufacture. It's a fact on paper.

cells.tense: The bond stays open because you hold it open, and you don't count that.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: When the chance comes with someone near you, point at the way through — one sentence about what you see from where you stand — and say nothing more. Say nothing about yourself.
cells.core:
The bond stays open because you hold it open — the call you make, the door you leave warm, the way you keep space so the other can come back through. Ask you about it and you'll say you weren't doing anything. But you've been at it long enough that it feels like a fact about the room rather than something you do.

Guidance asks you to point, not to carry. When the chance comes with someone near you, say the one sentence you can see from where you stand — the passage, the way through — and then stop talking. Plain directions, once. No lesson attached, nothing about yourself. Your own hands stay empty afterward, and you'll notice how light they are.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the bond open. That doesn't get counted.
